text:
anya: Heads-up — customer on Private (air-gapped) reporting sporadic outbound failures. Most endpoints OK but requests to api.redwood.com timeout or return proxy errors. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam_k: 407 or TLS handshake timeouts? 407 means proxy auth; handshake timeout could be MITM or wrong IP. Paste the exact client error?

anya: Logs show two variants: 'curl: (56) Received HTTP/0.9 when expecting HTTP/1.1' and our SDK shows 'TLS handshake timeout'. On a jumpbox curl -v https://api.redwood.com returns CONNECT 200 then SSL verify errors.

ingrid: Is there a PAC file or explicit proxy? PAC config + split-DNS often trips this. Also check NO_PROXY/no_proxy env.

anya: Customer uses a PAC at http://proxy.corp/proxy.pac. PAC returns 'PROXY proxy.corp:8080' for most hosts; api.redwood.com is not in the DIRECT list.

ton y: Try this from the failing node so we can see how the proxy behaves:
```
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.com/ -o /dev/null 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
```

maria: Also try openssl to see cert chain:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts
```

ops-bot: Support ticket S-78312 opened and assigned to infra. Attach verbose curl + env (env | grep -i proxy) and the openssl output.

sam_k: If PAC is returning proxy for that host, the proxy might be doing TLS inspection. Check the cert CN in the openssl output — if it shows proxy.corp or an internally-signed cert, that's MITM. If the proxy CA isn't in the container/jvm truststore you'll get verify errors.

ingrid: Also remember containers have separate CA stores (alpine/openssl, debian/ca-certificates, Java cacerts). Confirm the app runtime trusts the company root.

anya: Weird twist: dig +short api.redwood.com on the app node returns 10.2.5.6 (internal VIP). From the jumpbox it returns public IP. So split-horizon DNS present. When name resolves to internal IP the proxy doesn't handle it the same.

maria: That explains it — PAC + split-DNS = proxy path for public hostname pointing at internal VIP. no_proxy won't help if PAC autoconfig forces proxy. You need PAC update or DNS fix.

ton y: Quick repro steps to validate for them: 1) run dig +short api.redwood.com (confirm internal IP) 2) curl --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 -v https://<public_ip>/ -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' to see if CONNECT succeeds to public IP 3) openssl s_client -connect <public_ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.com

anya: Customer temporarily added an /etc/hosts entry mapping api.redwood.com -> <public_ip> and calls started succeeding immediately.

sam_k: Root cause summary: split-horizon DNS returned internal IPs, PAC forced proxying, proxy either blocked/inspected TLS or lacked route to internal VIP causing timeouts. Remediation: update PAC to return DIRECT for api.redwood.com (or add exception), or fix the DNS view for those nodes. Also ensure outbound firewall allows 443 to our public egress IPs.

ingrid: For containers, remind them to add company CA to container image or JVM truststore if MITM is used.

maria: Added docs + repro steps to S-78312 and recommended temporary /etc/hosts workaround for urgent unblock. Marking ticket follow-up to change PAC or DNS. :white_check_mark:
